findings.changed_text: 53% of people repeat. I bet you will.
findings.problem: The 'mind-read moment' announcement is self-contradictory and unbudgeted. 'The bot calls its shots out loud' (What Makes This Cool) and the sample line 'You just lost. 53% of people repeat. I bet you will.' are future-tense predictions, yet Round flow puts the announcement in step 4, the Reveal, after the throw. Spoken after the throw, 'I bet you will' is stale and 'You just lost' is false when the player won; spoken before the throw, it telegraphs the locked prediction to the player and audience, which invites a primed classmate to break the habit and changes what the demo measures. The stage round budget (3 s countdown, capture and reveal 1.5 s or less, taunt 2 s or less, 1 s pause) has no slot for it: the 11-word line takes roughly 3 to 4 s and could add about 5 to 15 s to the 65 s match, and the text does not say whether it replaces or adds to the six-word taunt.
findings.remedy: Decide when the line is spoken (during Lock or Countdown, or as a past-tense line at the Reveal such as 'Called it: you repeated after a loss'), whether telegraphing the prediction is acceptable, and whether it replaces or adds to the taunt; then put its duration into the stage round budget and the run sheet.

findings.problem: The Personal brain is defined, but not exactly. findings.remedy: Reduce it to one context variable or state the redundancy, state the tie-break used by tools/personal_check.py, describe it in the viva as a conditional-frequency table related to Naive Bayes, and write 'the player's last move' in the shift rule.

Practice matches run 20 rounds, so their win rate includes later, better-informed rounds and is not the 8-round stage expectation.
